plan: My private value is $25. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. This means bidding $25 ensures I only win if the prize is worth more to me than what others bid. If I win, I'll pay less than my valuation. If I lose, I miss out on potential profit. With no previous round history and values drawn independently, a true-value bid seems most rational.

With a private value of $18, my goal is to maximize potential profit. Since the second-highest bid determines my payment if I win, I want to bid strategically. Given the random nature and single round, I'll bid slightly above my value to increase winning chances, but not so high that I risk significant loss. A bid around $20-$22 seems optimal - giving me a buffer above my value while not overcommitting.

My private value is $31. To maximize profit, I want to win only if I can do so without paying more than my value. Given three bidders and random values, I'll bid strategically near my value. I'll bid $30.50 - slightly below my true value to create a buffer. This allows me to potentially win if others bid lower, while protecting against overpaying. The goal is to capture profit if my bid wins without risking more than the item is worth to me.
